bad: He couldn't have said how long he had slept, only that it hadn't been nearly enough. He had gone down into sleep the way a stone goes down into a well — heavily, gratefully, with no bottom to it that he could find. Out of that black water he was hauled all at once by a sound: a harsh, jangling, iron summons, a servants' bell rung somewhere above him with a violence that tore through the silence of the house and the deeper silence of his sleep together, the way a saw tears through green wood. He came up out of it with a cry he had no permission to make and started upright. A cruel rap to the crown of his head reminded him at once that he was no longer a free man with a ceiling a comfortable distance above his bed, but a thing folded away in a crawl-space scarcely the size of a child. It was behind the panelling behind his mistress's bed, with bare stone for a floor and her cast-off linen for a mattress, and not height enough in it to sit a man up straight. He had not yet learned the dimensions of his own confinement. That night, the lesson was delivered on his skull. The horrors of the day before came bleeding back into him gradually, the way colour bleeds back into a room at dawn — the salon, the canes passed hand to hand, the feet he had been made to worship, the new name hung about him, the small fouled breeches put into his mouth at the last, and the panel shut and barred on him from outside. The whole monstrous unlikeliness of his situation rose up again so fresh, so unaccountable, that for a moment the tears came on their own and ran sideways off his face onto the stone.
good: He couldn't have said how long he had slept, only that it hadn't been nearly enough. He came up out of it with a cry he had no permission to make and started upright. A cruel rap to the crown of his head reminded him of the limited size of his new bed chamber.

bad:
Then his tongue moved and found his mouth empty, and the tears stopped cold, frozen at their source by a fear sharper than any grief. The soiled cloth was gone from between his teeth. It had been a private study of his mistress's taste and scent, given to him to sleep on, and he was on no account to put it out until a better one drew it forth. Now it had worked loose in his sleep. The dark in that hole was absolute, and he couldn't see his own hand. So, with his heart going like the bell that had woken him, he dropped to his hands and knees on the cold stone and searched — patting, sweeping, scrabbling among the heaped cast-offs — in an agony in case the maid should come and find the thing fallen, and charge him for the finding in stripes.
He came on it at last, still damp with what he chose to believe was his own spit. He thrust it back into his mouth, and the foul taste of it filled him up barely a heartbeat before a thin line of light showed at the edge of the barred panel. The panel itself didn't open. Whoever had rung had not yet come. He had been spared, this once, by the breadth of a single instant — which was, he was learning, the whole margin his days were now to be lived on.
good: He remembered something. His tongue moved and found his now empty mouth, the soiled cloth gone from between his teeth. It must have worked itself loose in his sleep. He needed to find it and fast. The dark in that hole was absolute, and he couldn't see his own hand. So, with his heart going like the bell that had woken him, he dropped to his hands and knees on the cold stone and searched — patting and sweeping with his hands. He came on it at last, still damp with what he chose to believe was his own spit. He thrust it back into his mouth, and the foul taste of it filled him up barely a heartbeat before the light came on.

bad:
He remembered then what his mistress had laid on him: that he was to be *ready* — shaved, washed, scented — before the maid ever arrived to fetch him, and that to be found otherwise would earn him a punishment beside which the evening just past would seem a mercy. So he set the small wall-tap running and, breathing hard against the shock of it, submerged his aching body beneath the stream, because there was only ever cold water here, never warm. That was how the labours of the new day began, and they weren't eased by the discovery that scrubbing soap at a scrotum still caged, swollen and savaged from the evening's sport, and at welts laid down not twelve hours since across his back and his caged front both, woke every one of those hurts to fresh and indignant life.
Then came the shaving. He could find no growth anywhere on him — there had scarcely been time for any — but he didn't dare gamble on his mistress's eye agreeing with his own, so he passed the blade over the whole of himself anyway, by feel, in the cold and the cramped dark. He rinsed, and at last he was ready to put on the scent.
good: Now the work was done, he tuned into his body. It was cramped and he desperately wanted to stretch, but the hole wouldn't let him stand. Its dimensions allowed him to kneel at best, so he knelt and started twisting his spine and arms in attempt to relieve the stress and warm up. With the seconds lengthening into minutes and the silence closing over him again like water, his mind began to run. Somewhere beyond this wall his mistress lay warm and deep in a featherbed, untroubled, fast asleep, while he was set here folded and aching, with her discarded panties in mouth. Was this really worth the roof over the head? He was a good gardener, and his mother had enjoyed the employ for as long as he remembered. Surely they could find another house.

bad: The panel sprang open without so much as a creak — better oiled, he thought wildly, than it was ever kept when it shut on him — and a figure stood framed in the low gap, the chamber behind it drowned in the veil of its darkness.
good: The panel sprang open without so much as a creak — better oiled, he thought wildly, than it was ever kept when it shut on him — and a figure stood framed in the low gap, the chamber behind it drowned in the veil of its darkness. His mind cleared immediately.

bad: The figure said nothing. It only put out a hand and made a short impatient motion with it: *out.* He crawled to the opening and through it, desperate beyond words just to unfold himself, to stretch the long ache out of his back. He was given no leave to do anything of the kind, because the figure had already turned its back on him and was filing away toward the chamber door without bothering to see whether he followed. All he was granted, in the passing, was one brief stolen glimpse of his mistress where she lay deep in her sleep, a soft contentment on her sleeping face, before he had to scramble up and tiptoe out at the figure's heel.
good: The figure said nothing. It only put out a hand and made a short impatient motion with it. He crawled to the opening and through it, desperate to finally stretch the long ache out of his back. But the figure had already turned its back and was filing away toward the chamber door. All he was granted, in the passing, was one brief stolen glimpse of his mistress where she lay deep in her sleep, a soft contentment on her sleeping face, before he had to scramble up and tiptoe out at the figure's heel.

bad: In the corridor the dim light of the wall-candles let him see at last who his guide was, and he knew her. It was one of the house-maids — Keziah — a slight, thin slip of a creature who went on ahead of him without a backward look, toward another door. He followed quick, the obedience his mistress had branded into him still burning, so vivid it seemed to lie just under his skin.
good: In the corridor the dim light of the wall-candles let him see at last who his guide was. It was one of the house-maids — Keziah — a slight, thin slip of a creature who went on ahead of him without a backward look, toward another door. The same one who trained the cane on his back during lunch the day before. He followed at heel.

bad: Two days ago this same Keziah had carried a cool jug down to him in the heat of the garden, and lingered to pass the time of day, one servant idling a friendly minute with another. A week ago — a week! a thing now lying on the far side of an ocean — when the young mistress had taken it into her head to ride out and eat on the grass, it had fallen to Keziah and Edmund together, the maid and the gardener, to go on ahead and spread the cloth and lay out the cold fowl and the fruit against her coming. They had been, in those days, of a rank: two servants of the one house, who might trade a joke or a grievance below stairs as equals. And here she went in front of him now, candle in hand, his keeper and his better. The whole dreadful arithmetic of the house had, in seven days, turned exactly over, so that the man who had stood as her equal was now set far beneath her, made to serve the very servant who had once served beside him.
good: Two days ago this same Keziah had carried a cool jug down to him in the heat of the garden, and lingered to pass the time of day, one servant idling a friendly minute with another. And a week ago, when the young mistress fancied a picnic on the ground, it had fallen to Keziah and Edmund together to go on ahead and prepare everything for her. They had been two servants of the one house, who might trade a joke or a grievance below stairs as equals. And here she went in front of him now as his keeper, because his mistress wished it so.

bad: Keziah shut the door behind them and stood square in front of him, taking her stock of him from the crown of his shaved head to his bare feet, slow, unhurried, the way a buyer looks over a beast at a fair. He stood naked in the candlelight and didn't know what to do with himself, or where to put his eyes, or how a thing in his condition was meant to hold its hands. The old humiliation came swelling up out of his belly again, and the blood came up hot into his cheeks. Keziah saw it and laughed.
good: Keziah shut the door behind them and stood square in front of him, taking stock of him from the crown of his shaved head to his bare feet, slow and unhurried. He stood naked in the candlelight and didn't know what to do with himself. The humiliation came swelling up out of his belly again, and the blood came up hot into his cheeks. Keziah saw it and laughed.

bad:
His body leapt to it before his mind had fully heard the word — the feet spread, the eyes cast down, the skirt that wasn't there lifted by hands that found nothing to lift, because he stood as bare as he had been born, presenting to her, plain and caged, the whole ruin of his situation. She walked a slow circuit around him, laying her hands on him here and there as though feeling for dust on a mantel. Behind him, he heard her draw in a considering breath at the scent of him, and on the whole she seemed satisfied with what she had found.
Last of all she came round and stood in front of him.
good: He obeyed before his mind had fully heard the word — the feet spread, the eyes cast down, hands folded behind his head. She walked a slow circuit around him, laying her hands on him here and there. She moved to stand behind his back and he heard her draw in large breath, smelling him. Finally, she came round and stood in front of him.

bad: He was thunderstruck for the briefest instant — *she* was a maid; she had carried his plates — but the breath of the hesitation had scarcely left him before the trained obedience overrode it and bore him down. He dropped to his knees and set his lips to the leather of her boot, to the dark stocking above it, and breathed in the warmth and the savour that came off them.
good: He hesitated for the briefest instant, but the short training he'd received the day before kicked in. He dropped to his knees and set his lips to the leather of her boot, to the dark stocking above it, and breathed in the warmth and the savour that came off them.

bad: 'Miss Victoria has had clothes laid out for you,' came the voice from above his bent head. 'Put them on. And be quick about it.' And Keziah laughed again, a small, dry, private laugh, to see the gardener of the house grovelling at her shoe-leather.
good: 'Lady Victoria has had clothes laid out for you,' came the voice from above his bent head. 'Put them on. And be quick about it.'

bad: He came to the clothes — the frilled and flounced dress, the pale stockings, the cruel built-up shoes — and found, to a kind of dull despair, that his hands knew the way of them a little better now than they had, and the dressing came easier. Only the shame in it didn't come easier, and wouldn't, he was beginning to suspect, ever come easier at all. Keziah watched the transformation work itself on him, and snickered once more when it was complete.
good: He approached to the clothes — the frilled dress, the pale stockings, the cruel built-up shoes. His hands knew the way of them a little better now, so the dressing came easier. The shame didn't dissapear however, and he was beginning to suspect it never would. Keziah watched him and snickered.

bad: He opened his mouth. He saw her fingers come toward it, felt them go in, and felt them make two or three small unnecessary motions there, pressing the damp cloth back and down toward his throat, gauging him, watching his face for what it would do. When at last he gagged on it, a satisfied little smile spread across her thin features, and she drew the thing out.
good: He opened his mouth. Her fingers came toward it and went in, made two or three small unnecessary motions, pressing the damp cloth back and down toward his throat, gauging him while watching the expression on face. When he gagged on it, a satisfied little smile spread across her thin features, and she drew the thing out.

bad: 'Wash your mouth, and look sharp,' she said. 'You've a full morning's work to get through before your mistress so much as stirs; and I can promise you, you'll not want to keep *her* waiting.' She drew an obvious and unhidden pleasure from saying it.
good: 'Wash your mouth, and look sharp,' she said. 'You've a full morning's work to get through before your mistress so much as stirs, and you won't want to keep *her* waiting.' She took an open pleasure in saying it.

bad: She led him down, and then down again, by a passage he had never in his life had occasion to take — because the gardener's world had been the open grounds and the kitchen step, never these buried inward regions — into the deep servants' quarters of the house. They were low, lime-washed, candle-smelling regions whose existence he had always known of in the abstract, the way one knows of the cellars beneath a city, and never once thought about. At the end of it she brought him into a room made of damp, and of a smell, and of clothing — mountains of clothing, it seemed to him, ranged and heaped and tumbled on every side, more than he had supposed the whole household could own.
good: She led him down, and then down again, by a passage he had never had occasion to take into the deep servants' quarters. They were low, lime-washed, candle-smelling rooms he had always known of in the abstract and never once thought about. At the end of the passage she brought him into a room full damp and smelly clothing. Mountains of it heaped and tumbled on every side, more than he had supposed the whole household could own.

bad: 'Welcome to the laundry,' said Keziah, with the bright civility of a hostess showing a guest the best room. 'Here is where the soiled linen of the entire house is gathered in, each night, from every chamber in it. You are to wash it — and mind the delicates in particular, for there is fine stuff in here that an idle pair of hands would ruin. You do know the way of so important a task?'
good: 'Welcome to the laundry,' said Keziah, with the bright civility of a hostess showing a guest the best room. 'Here is where the soiled linen of the entire house is gathered each night. You are to wash it. Mind the delicates in particular, for there is fine stuff in here that an idle pair of hands would ruin. You do know the way of so important a task?'

bad: A rod was in her hand — he couldn't have said where it came from, so quickly did it appear — and Keziah, slight little figure that she was, took her swing and laid it across him hard, and the lash fell on his face.
good: A rod was in her hand — he couldn't have said where it came from, it appeared so quickly — and slight as she was, Keziah took her swing and laid it across him hard. The lash fell on his face.

bad: 'A pretty girl like you, with those soft little hands — well, it's no wonder,' she said, and laughed. 'Here. I'll show you the once.'
good: 'A pretty girl like you, it's no wonder,' she said, and laughed. 'Here. I'll show you just this once'

bad:
She showed him — briefly, carelessly, in the manner of someone who means the instruction to fall just short of enough — and then went out and left him there alone among the reeking heaps, in despair, with no idea on earth of when, or whether, they would come for him again. But there was no room left in his day for self-pity, so he bent his back to the work, as he had been instructed.
The door was shut now, and no other woman near. And here, alone among the suds and the steam, with the work and the shame all her own and shared with no one, it was the maid Trixy who laboured.
good: She showed him carelessly, and then went out, leaving him alone among the reeking heaps, with no idea when anyone would come for him again. But there was no room in his day for self-pity so he bent his back to the work.

bad:
One garment after another passed through her hands, and as she scrubbed, the harsh soap began to take its revenge on her — biting at the raw skin of her wrists, creeping somehow into her eyes and stinging there until she worked half-blind. Through that smarting blur she came, item by item, on things she knew for women's: fine things, intimate things, that could belong to none below the family. She lifted one to her face — already a half-formed habit, the trained reflex of a nose set lately to its schooling — and breathed. To her own dismay, she knew the scent of it. It was her owner's. It was the scent of the very person who had decided her fate and now governed each breath she drew, and she found she had learned it well enough, in a single day, to swear to it among a hundred others.
She took a particular care over the cleaning of that one before she set it by.
A moment later her hands closed on another such garment — coarser, this one, and plainer, the honest hard-worn linen of someone who labours below stairs — and she knew that scent too, knew it to the very marrow, though she had not breathed it so near since she was a child at the knee. It was her own mother's. Her mother had been one of the household's maids for thirty years, and her poor washing was gathered into the same great heap as all the rest. And here a thing happened in him that he was ashamed of afterward, and couldn't undo: the man who had been Edmund, kneeling at his wash-tub, caught himself committing even that dear and familiar scent deliberately to memory — drawing it in, turning it over, laying it away on some shelf inside him against the day he should need to know it — as though his own mother were now not a person to be loved, with a face he might look on, but a smell to be catalogued among the laundry. Which was, he understood dimly, exactly the use the house meant to put her to, and him, and all the love that had ever passed between them.
good: One garment after another passed through his hands. The harsh soap started biting at the raw skin of his wrists, creeping into his eyes and stinging until he worked half-blind. His hands followed the pattern, picking the next item, soaking it, giving it a sharp wave to let the water drip and hanging it up on the clothes line. Suddenly his fingers came acress a fine, intimate thing that could belong to none other than his Mistress. He lifted it to her face and breathed. He recognized the scent. It was Victoria's. He took a particular care while cleaning that one.

bad: He had no idea how much of the morning was gone — there was no clock in that low room, and the house's clocks, ticking on somewhere above in their elderly, disapproving way, didn't trouble to count the hours for the likes of him — when he heard the door creak open. He sank at once into the *Greet*, knowing better by now than to be caught standing for a single second. Keziah came in and took her stock of the room, as did he, after his own permitted fashion, with his gaze fixed firmly on the floor. At the lower edge of his sight he saw that the heaps of clothing had visibly gone down.
good: He had no idea how much of the morning was gone when he heard the door creak open. He sank at once to his knees. Keziah came in and took stock of the room and the fruit of the labour. The heaps of laundry that had littered the room now hung, fresh and fragrant, on a web of clothes lines.

bad: Keziah took a step and stood in front of him, and put out her foot. The toe of her boot slid forward and came to rest against his caged groin, and wiggled there a while, she enjoying herself with an open and leisurely relish.
good: Keziah took a step and stood in front of him and put out her foot. The toe of her boot slid forward and came to rest against his caged groin, and wiggled there a while, with an open, leisurely relish.

bad: The tears stood in his eyes already, in plain anticipation of what was coming, but he obeyed her on the instant, without the breadth of a pause. Keziah took a step or two, surveying what he had offered up to her. Then he felt the bamboo trace itself gently down across his buttocks and slide into the cleft between them, almost — God forgive him — a caress. What came after was no caress.
good: Keziah took a step or two, surveying what he had offered up. Then the bamboo traced gently down across his buttocks and slid into the cleft between them, almost — God forgive him — a caress. What came after was no caress.

bad: But she wasn't minded to keep to his backside alone, because soon enough the strokes came scattering down across his bared legs, his knees, wherever the rod chose to land, so that he bucked and swayed and could scarcely keep his place. Keep it he did, though, too afraid of a fiercer reckoning to let his pose go for an instant.
good: This time she wasn't planning to keep to his backside alone. The strokes came scattering down across his bared legs, his knees, wherever the rod chose to land, so that he bucked and swayed and could scarcely keep his place.

bad: 'Straighten up, and follow me,' said Keziah, as composed as though nothing whatever had passed between them. He drew the pale stockings up from around his ankles and followed his tormentor. 'Your mistress will wake before long, and her breakfast is got ready,' she explained as they came into the kitchen. 'You are to carry it up to her room and serve it to her.'
good: 'Straighten up, and follow me,' said Keziah, as composed as if nothing had passed between them. He drew the pale stockings up from around his ankles and followed her. 'The Lady will wake before long, and her breakfast is ready,' she said as they came into the kitchen. 'You're to carry it up to her room and serve it to her.'

bad: The smells of that kitchen rolled over him as he came into it, and his belly turned within him at the warmth and the wonder of them. They put him cruelly in mind of the soured, soggy remnants he had been given to lap from the bowl the day before — the last thing he had been allowed to eat — and woke in him a hunger so sharp, a thirst so parching, that for a moment he could think of nothing else. Yet he didn't dare breathe a word of either. A silver tray stood ready, laid out with delicacies: fruit, and ham, and pastry fresh and flaking from the oven. Keziah lifted it as lightly as a hat and laid it across his outstretched arms.
good: The smells of the kitchen rolled over him as he came in. His belly turned at the warmth and wonder of them. They put him cruelly in mind of the soured, soggy remnants he had lapped from the bowl the day before — the last thing he had been allowed to eat — and woke a hunger so sharp, a thirst so parching, that for a moment he could think of nothing else. A silver tray stood ready, laid with delicacies: fruit, ham and a pastry fresh and flaking from the oven. Keziah lifted it and laid it across his outstretched arms.

bad: He crept up the stairs with great care, in dread of waking some treacherous creak out of a board, and came to his mistress's chamber. There he set the tray down on the floor and eased the door open. She lay still fast asleep. He took the tray up again, slid himself inside, and shut the door without a sound. Then, quick but soundless, he took his place at the side of the bed and waited.
good: He crept up the stairs with great care, in dread of waking a creak out of some treacherous board, and came to his mistress's chamber. She lay fast asleep. Quick but silent, he took his place at the side of the bed and waited.

bad: The fruit, the ham, the fresh pastry breathed up their wonders at him, and his stomach, betraying its master past all control, let out all at once a long, deep, rolling moan, the cry of a body too long denied. He stood petrified. It had been *loud*. Had it woken her? He stole a look. No — Miss Victoria slept on, undisturbed. But the thing wasn't done with him. Another churn came rolling up, and he shifted his pose against it, and shifted in vain, because another escaped, and then another, his own treacherous flesh announcing his hunger to the silent room as plainly as a bell.
good: The fruit, the ham, the fresh pastry sent up their smells at him, and his stomach, betraying its master past all control, let out a long, deep, rolling moan, the cry of a body too long denied. He stood petrified. It had been *loud*. Had it woken her? He stole a look. No — Miss Victoria slept on, undisturbed. But it wasn't done with him. Another churn came rolling up; he shifted his pose against it, and shifted in vain, because another escaped, and then another, his own treacherous flesh announcing his hunger to the silent room as plainly as a bell.

bad: 'Present' she snapped; and as he drew up his skirt she took the first bite of a flaking pastry. The smell of it broke over him fresh, his stomach gave out its loud and helpless complaint, and Victoria smiled at the sound, savouring this small unbidden tribute the torment paid her on its own. She made no remark on it, but went on eating. Then, all at once, she put out her hand and fell to playing idly with the caged weight between his legs, twisting at it, tickling it, breaking off only when she needed the second hand to spread her butter, and taking the brutal little game up again the moment the butter was spread, a cat playing with a mouse. Edmund stood and bore it, having no choice in the world but to bear his mistress's whims.
good: 'Present' she snapped; and as he drew up his skirt while she took the first bite of a flaking pastry. The crunch of it between her teeth, combined with the intoxicating smell, caused his stomach to churn loudly. Victoria smiled at the sound, savouring this small torture, and continued eating. Then, all at once, she put out her hand and fell to playing idly with the caged weight between his legs, twisting at it, tickling it. She broke it off for a moment when she needed the second hand to spread her butter, and quickly picked up where she left off. Edmund stood and bore it, having no choice but to bear his mistress's whims.

bad: He had no choice but to take the pot to his food.
good: He turned around and moved towards the bowls.
